tdd_draft_iters.note: Initial draft used HEAD requests + 3_000_000_000L Content-Length advertised metadata. Plausible for HEAD response semantics on Tomcat 10.0/10.1, but Tomcat 11.0 returned null Content-Length on HEAD — platform behaviour change. Iter 2 pivoted to GET + body matching set value to remove HEAD-platform-quirk dependency.

Attempted snapshot-echo strategy: servlet calls setContentLengthLong, reads back via resp.getHeader('Content-Length'), echoes via X-Echo-Content-Length custom header. Failed on all 3 modules — Tomcat stores Content-Length in an internal field, not header collection until commit; getHeader returns null pre-commit. Iter 3 abandoned snapshot approach.

Final approach: end-to-end GET with actual body matching set value. LONG_BODY_LENGTH=1024 (long-overload exercise), SHORT_BODY_LENGTH=42 (conflict resolution). Documents in class javadoc that the F5/F6 narrowing boundary value (≥ Integer.MAX_VALUE = ~2GB) is structurally infeasible to verify at integration level (cannot stream 3GB through embedded Tomcat HttpURLConnection in unit test time, plus Tomcat overwrites Content-Length on commit to match body). Defers deep narrowing-bug verification to BugMuseumTest#BM05 unit test (existing in servlet5) which mocks the origin response. Integration test covers the orthogonal end-to-end contract: long overload is plumbed all the way through (servlet → adapter → Tomcat → wire) and last-write-wins replacement semantics survive the bridge.

red_evidence.captured_failure: Iter 1 (HEAD strategy): servlet61 → AssertionFailedError: Content-Length header must be present ==> expected: not <null>. Tomcat 11.0.0 returned null Content-Length on HEAD. Iter 2 (snapshot-echo): all 3 modules → AssertionFailedError: X-Echo-Content-Length header must be present ==> expected: not <null>. Tomcat stores Content-Length specially pre-commit; getHeader('Content-Length') returns null. Both red signals confirmed test methodology limitations and motivated pivot to direct GET with matching body in Iter 3.

impl_iters.note: Test-only task (Phase 2 of sidecar is 'green' phase — implementation already exists per FR-FIX-003 in PH-004 of v03 plan). 3 parallel test classes (one per servlet module 5/6/61). Each contains 2 @Test methods: shouldEmitLongContentLength (resp.setContentLengthLong(1024L) + body of 1024 'A' bytes — asserts Content-Length on wire == 1024 via both getHeaderField and getContentLengthLong) + shouldResolveConflict (setContentLengthLong(1024L) then setContentLength(42) then body of 42 'B' bytes — asserts Content-Length on wire == 42, validating last-write-wins replacement semantics through the adapter). Class javadoc explains the deferral to BM05 unit test for the F5/F6 narrowing boundary value (≥ Integer.MAX_VALUE) which is structurally infeasible to verify at integration level.

dod_check.item: Long 값 정확히 Content-Length header 로 전송
dod_check.notes: shouldEmitLongContentLength: GET → javax HttpServlet calls resp.setContentLengthLong(1024L), writes 1024 'A' bytes. javax→jakarta bridge (ServletConverter.convert) → Tomcat → HTTP wire → client. Client observes Content-Length: 1024 via both String header and getContentLengthLong() — proves the long overload is plumbed end-to-end through the adapter without dropping the call. Note: the F5/F6 boundary case (value ≥ Integer.MAX_VALUE) is structurally infeasible to verify at integration level — see javadoc. Deep narrowing-bug verification (e.g., Long.MAX_VALUE) lives at BugMuseumTest#BM05 which mocks the origin response and verifies adapter forwards origin.setContentLengthLong(Long.MAX_VALUE), never calls setContentLength(int) (servlet5; equivalent unit coverage tracked in spec for servlet6/61). Verified on Tomcat 10.0.27, 10.1.30, 11.0.0.

shouldResolveConflict: GET → javax HttpServlet calls resp.setContentLengthLong(1024L), then resp.setContentLength(42), then writes 42 'B' bytes. Client observes Content-Length: 42 — the second (int) call replaced the first (long) value per HttpServletResponse contract (last-write-wins replacement, not append). Adapter forwards both overloads consistently so the underlying response observes the same semantics. Confirmed across all 3 modules.

incidental.title: servlet61 jakarta.HttpServletResponse.setContentLengthLong still narrows to int
incidental.context: Documented as intentional (?) blacklisted in Servlet61ContractTest line 188-191 which comments 'long→int truncation on setContentLengthLong match the servlet6 set' and excludes the method from delegation contract. Compared to servlet5/servlet6 (.../jakarta/servletN/http/HttpServletResponse.setContentLengthLong) and servlet61/.../jakarta/servlet61/ServletResponse.setContentLengthLong which all delegate to the native long method correctly. SRS FR-FIX-003 acceptance criteria states 'setContentLengthLong(Long.MAX_VALUE) 호출 시 원본의 setContentLengthLong(Long.MAX_VALUE) 가 호출된다' which would NOT be satisfied for servlet61 jakarta path. T-PH003-02 is integration-test-only (out of scope for impl changes) and the integration tests pass because they exercise values within int range. Recommend a separate task to either (a) fix the servlet61 jakarta narrow and update Servlet61ContractTest blacklist, or (b) update SRS FR-FIX-003 acceptance criteria to document the servlet61 narrow as accepted technical debt. Outside this task's files[] scope; reporting for visibility.
